To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the relative abundances of the different morphotypes of the plexus Globigerinoidesspp. are highly sensitive to changes in the position of the Azores Front Current system (AFCS) during the last 75 kyr.

1) the G. ruberg. kummerform group was the most abundant morphotype of the G. rubber – G. elongatasp. during the last glacial cycle, 2) G. elongatus was the dominant morphotype of the plexus during interglacials and 3) the G. rubber cyclostoma type was the dominant morph during glacials.
the G. rubers.s. and G. rubers. cyclostoma type morphotypes were the dominant taxa in the Azores during the glacial periods of MIS 5, MIS 4 and MIS 2.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the distribution and ecology of the G. elongatus - G. ruber morphotypes in the North Atlantic during the last 75 kyr, which is a critical period to understand the evolution of the STG/AC system.
the distribution of G. ruber morphotypes in the STG and the Azores Front region and their relationship with environmental changes in the last 74 kyr.
the distribution and ecology of the G. elongatus - G. ruber morphotypes during the late Pleiostocene-Holocene in the Azores area.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the G. rubert – G. elongata s.l. assemblages in the Azores area were mainly controlled by the position of the STG/AC boundary and the relative abundance of the morphotypes was mainly controlled by the temperature of the surface waters.

the G. rubers.s. morphotype is a warm water taxon that prefers the STG, while G. elongatus and G. elongatuscf.1 preferentially live in the AC, and G. elongatuscyclostoma type is a cold water taxon restricted to the AC.
the G. rubers.s. morphotypes are more tolerant to cold conditions than G. elongatus morphotypes and that the G. elongatus species is more adapted to the warmest conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
G. elongatus is more abundant in the STG, whereas the G. rubecyclostoma type is more abundant in AC.
the G. rubercyclostoma type is more adapted to cold and nutrient rich waters than the other G. ruber morphotypes and G. elongatus.

the G. rubercyclostoma type is the most suitable proxy to reconstruct the position occupied by STG/AC during the late Pleisto-Holocene, while the G. elongatus morphotype is a proxy to track the STG/AC boundary during glacial periods.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the position of the STG/AFCS was located south of the present-day position during the last interglacial and glacial periods, and it was located north of the present-day location during the last two deglaciations.
